title: Validate amounts and account references
prompt: A raw feed carries rows the books can't take: a negative amount, a currency code nobody uses, a transaction for an account the bank doesn't have, or no account at all. Write `valid_transactions(transactions, accounts)`. It starts from your `transaction_view(transactions)` and keeps only the rows that pass every check below.
rules: `amount` is more than 0. A missing, zero or negative amount fails.
`account_id` is an account in `accounts`. A missing `account_id` fails.
`currency` is that account's own currency, written exactly the same. Any other currency, or none, fails.
Return `transaction_view`'s columns, in the same order. Checking an account never adds a row, and repeated rows stay for now: the next step removes them.
hints: Start with `view = transaction_view(transactions)` and filter `F.col("amount") > 0`. A missing amount fails any comparison on its own.
A left semi join keeps the rows that have a match, without adding columns or copies. Join `accounts.select("account_id", "currency")` on both columns and the two account checks happen at once.
A join on a list of columns moves those columns to the front. Finish with `.select(*view.columns)` to put them back in order.
explanation: `filter(F.col("amount") > 0)` drops negative, zero and missing amounts in one test, because a comparison with NULL is never true. The account checks are a left semi join on `account_id` and `currency` together: a row survives only if some account has that id and that currency, so orphans, rows with no account and rows in the wrong or an unknown currency all go. A semi join adds no columns and never repeats a row, even if an account were listed twice; an inner join would do both. Checking only that the currency is one of USD, EUR or GBP would let a euro payment onto a pound account. Repeated rows are left alone here so that the next step can remove them on purpose.
